To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of corals in eastern Australia is determined by a number of interacting factors.

(1) the latitudinal distribution of coral reefs is limited by a number of factors that act in concert; (2) coral communities in the subtropics are dominated by coralline algae, macroalgae and corallimorphs rather than corals; (3) coral cover and diversity are lower in the subtropies than in the Great Barrier Reef; (4) there are major changes in the composition and structure of coral communities at around 28°S; and

1) coral cover and community structure change dramatically along a latitudinal gradient in eastern Australia, and 2) this is due to a number of interacting factors, including water temperature, aragnonite saturation, light, and competition with algae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and understanding the factors that regulate the distributional limits and community structure of corals and coral reef ecosystems.
the following questions: (1) What is the nature of the latitudinal changes that occur in the distribution and abundance of corals and coral communities?
the biophysical factors that determine the distribution and community structure of corals and reefs at the limits of the coral reef biogeographic province.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the latitudinal limits of coral reefs are determined by a combination of biotic and abiotic factors, and that the relative importance of each factor is dependent on the location.
the latitudinal distribution of coral reefs is determined by the combined effects of water temperature and light, with water temperature having a more dominant role.
the distribution of corals is determined by the interaction of multiple factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the distribution of coral reefs in eastern Australia is determined by a combination of factors that include: (1) temperature, (2) water clarity, (3) light availability, (4) water motion, (5) competition between corals, macroalgae and other biota, (6) coral growth rates, (7) coral reproduction and recruitment, (8) coral community structure, (9) coral species diversity, (10) larval connectivity and (11) reef accretion
the latitudinal changes observed in coral communities and reefs in eastern Australia are a result of the combined effects of water temperature, arago nite saturation and light availability.
the Great Barrier Reef is the northernmost limit of coral reefs, and the subtropical reefs are the southernmost limit of coral-dominated communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the distribution of corals and coral communities in eastern Australian waters can be understood by considering the interplay between the biophysical environment and the biology of corals, and by considering how corals interact with other benthos.
latitudinal changes to community structure are not simply the result of a single environmental variable.
coral communities at the northern and southern extremes of their distribution are not necessarily representative of coral communities at intermediate latitudes.
